fml.menu.mods.info.description.starrysky: A more beautiful night sky: more stars, varied sizes and colors, gentle twinkling and shooting stars. Client-side only.
starrysky.configuration.title: Starry Sky Configuration
starrysky.configuration.enabled.tooltip: Turns the improved night sky on or off.
starrysky.configuration.starCount.toolti: Number of stars on the celestial sphere. Vanilla shows about 800. The Milky Way adds twice as many tiny stars on top. Even 10000 stays cheap to draw.
starrysky.configuration.starSize.tooltip: Size multiplier applied to every star.
starrysky.configuration.coloredStars.too: Adds subtle color variations: white, bluish and pale yellow stars.
starrysky.configuration.twinkle.tooltip: Makes the stars gently twinkle over time.
starrysky.configuration.shootingStars.to: Occasional shooting stars streak across the night sky.
starrysky.configuration.shootingStarFreq: Average number of shooting stars per minute on a clear night. 0 disables them.
starrysky.configuration.milkyWay.tooltip: A glowing band of star dust crosses the night sky. This is the most demanding effect of the mod, although still light: turn it off first if the game slows down when you look at the night sky.
starrysky.configuration.auroras.tooltip: Curtains of green and violet light dance in the northern sky at night, only in cold biomes (snow, ice).
starrysky.configuration.telescope.toolti: Aim a spyglass at a bright star at night to see its name and characteristics.
starrysky.configuration.planets.tooltip: Venus, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn: bright, steady points that move from one night to the next. Venus shows up near the horizon at dusk or dawn.
starrysky.configuration.meteorShowers.to: About one night in ten, many more shooting stars. Announced at dusk.
starrysky.configuration.moonHalo.tooltip: A soft glow around the moon, stronger at full moon. A full moon also makes the stars and the Milky Way a little paler.
starrysky.configuration.hideCloudsAtNigh: Clouds gradually fade away as night falls and come back at dawn, so nothing hides the stars. They stay when it rains or snows.
starrysky.journal.title: Observation Journal
starrysky.journal.empty: Nothing observed yet. At night, hold a spyglass on a bright star or a planet for a moment to add it here.
starrysky.shower.announce: A meteor shower lights up the sky tonight
starrysky.telescope.hint.too_bright: The sky is too bright to see the stars
starrysky.configuration.hideVanillaStars: Hides Minecraft's original stars wherever Starry Sky is active.
starrysky.configuration.dimensions.toolt: Dimension IDs where Starry Sky is active (e.g. minecraft:overworld). Only dimensions with a normal sky are affected: the Nether and the End stay unchanged.
starrysky.configuration.comets.tooltip: Every now and then, a comet stays visible for a few nights: a bright nucleus, a greenish coma and two tails (golden dust and blue ions) always pointing away from the sun. Aim at it with a spyglass to add it to your journal!
starrysky.configuration.eclipses.tooltip: On some full-moon nights, the moon darkens and turns copper red around midnight. The darker sky makes the stars stand out.
starrysky.eclipse.announce: A lunar eclipse will happen tonight, around midnight
starrysky.comet.announce: Comet %s is visible in the sky
starrysky.achievement.first_light.desc: Observe your first sky object with a spyglass
starrysky.achievement.planets.desc: Observe Venus, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn
starrysky.achievement.figure.desc: Observe every star of a constellation
starrysky.achievement.comet.desc: Observe a comet with a spyglass
starrysky.achievement.eclipse.desc: Look at the moon during a total eclipse
starrysky.achievement.master.desc: Observe every object in the sky
